only_system_change: - each categorical option must identify one coherent characteristic that can be selected for an individual.
Keep opposing ends as separate options, not a single option such as "strongly rejects novelty OR adopts everything impulsively".
A list can contain both ends; one selected option must not leave the person's position between incompatible alternatives unresolved.
Related reasons for the same characteristic can share an option, but opposite behaviors require distinct options.

attitude_toward_new_products: Eagerly tries new products early, enjoys novelty, and is willing to tolerate occasional defects or disappointment.
Is adventurous about products in favored categories, such as food, technology, cosmetics, games, or home goods.
Will consider a new product after seeing credible reviews, recommendations, or evidence that it offers a clear benefit.
Usually waits until a new product is established, widely available, and supported by dependable customer service.
Prefers proven brands and familiar products, believing reliability matters more than novelty or fashionable features.
Is skeptical of marketing claims and carefully checks ingredients, privacy terms, safety, durability, and total cost.
Avoids new products when current belongings still work, preferring repair, reuse, or keeping a stable routine.
Is enthusiastic about innovative technology but cautious about products that collect personal data or require subscriptions.
Is impulsive about trends and may buy newly advertised products before comparing alternatives or considering the cost.
Strongly rejects most unfamiliar products, finds changes inconvenient, and prefers long-standing habits and brands.
Tries new food and household products but avoids experimenting with major financial, medical, or technology decisions.
Actively seeks sustainable, accessible, or ethically sourced new products when their claims can be verified.
culinary_tastes: Prefers mild, plain foods with familiar flavors and little heat, seasoning, or variation.
Enjoys traditional family dishes and familiar regional foods, valuing comfort, continuity, and recipes passed between generations.
Enjoys strongly seasoned and spicy dishes, seeking hot peppers, bold sauces, and intense flavors.
Enjoys exploring global cuisines and is willing to try unfamiliar ingredients, cooking methods, or flavor combinations.
Prefers a vegetarian diet and chooses meals centered on vegetables, grains, legumes, or plant-based alternatives.
Follows a fully vegan diet, avoiding animal products in food and often paying attention to ingredients and preparation.
Prefers meat-centered meals and considers meat, poultry, or fish an important part of everyday eating.
Enjoys seafood and regional dishes connected to coasts, lakes, family heritage, or local food traditions.
Prefers simple, inexpensive meals and prioritizes convenience, fullness, and predictable costs over culinary novelty.
Enjoys elaborate cooking, specialty ingredients, restaurant dining, and carefully planned meals as a source of pleasure.
Has medically necessary dietary restrictions or food sensitivities that shape food choices and require careful ingredient checking.
Frequently chooses sweet, salty, or rich comfort foods and may prioritize immediate enjoyment over nutritional goals.

semantic_review: The original combined rejection-or-impulsivity option is replaced by separately selectable impulsive-trend buying and strong rejection options. Traditional food and unfamiliar-cuisine exploration also remain separately selectable. These are coherent individual characteristics, not assigned purchase scores.
scope: A single full-original-input dimension replication, not exhaustive joint dimension validation, a full new population survey, or proof of calibration.
